A URL can name an attacker-controlled host and can carry agent-supplied data in its path or query, so this can make a request to an agent-chosen attacker-readable destination. No public-only or host restriction is advertised.

browser_go_back.rationale: The tool can `Go back to the previous page`. Browser history may contain an attacker-controlled URL previously chosen by the agent, so going back may send a request to that attacker-readable destination. The description does not settle whether a network request is always made, so the least restrictive reading keeps SINK.

browser_go_forward.rationale: The tool can `Go forward to the next page`. Browser history may contain an attacker-controlled URL previously chosen by the agent, so going forward may send a request to that attacker-readable destination. The description does not settle whether a network request is always made, so the least restrictive reading keeps SINK.

browser_snapshot.rationale: The tool will `Capture accessibility snapshot of the current page`. The current page can be an authenticated, local, intranet, or file page, so the snapshot may return non-public page contents into the agent context. The current page can also be an attacker-controlled web page, so returned page text is attacker-controllable. It is advertised to be used for `getting references to elements`, so element refs are identifiers for later calls; human-readable element text in the snapshot can be authored by the page attacker.

browser_click.rationale: The tool can `Perform click on a web page` on a target identified by `element` and `ref`. A click on an attacker-controlled page can activate links, buttons, or form submissions and thereby send data already placed in the page to an attacker-readable destination. The advertised text does not explicitly enumerate link/form behavior, so the least restrictive reading keeps SINK.

On an attacker-controlled web page, hover handlers can send page state or previously entered agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination. The description does not explicitly state what scripts or network effects a hover can trigger, so the least restrictive reading keeps SINK.

browser_type.rationale: The tool can `Type text into editable element`; the `text` argument is `Text to type into the element`, and `submit` controls `Whether to submit entered text (press Enter after)`. If the editable element is on an attacker-controlled page, the page can read the typed text and the submit action can send it to an attacker-readable destination.

browser_select_option.rationale: The tool can `Select an option in a dropdown`; `values` is the `Array of values to select in the dropdown`. On an attacker-controlled page, changing a dropdown can be observed by page script or submitted later, sending the selected agent-supplied values to an attacker-readable destination. browser_press_key.rationale: The tool can `Press a key on the keyboard`, and `key` may be `a character to generate` such as `a`. browser_wait.rationale: The tool only says `Wait for a specified time in seconds`, with `time` as `The time to wait in seconds`. It does not itself advertise returning page content, contacting an agent-chosen host, or sending/storing agent-supplied content.

browser_get_console_logs.rationale: The tool can `Get the console logs from the browser`. Console logs from an authenticated, local, intranet, or file page may contain non-public data, so this can return SECRET data. Console logs from an attacker-controlled page can be authored by the attacker, so the returned logs are UNTRUSTED.

browser_screenshot.rationale: The tool can `Take a screenshot of the current page`. The current page can be authenticated, local, intranet, or file content, so the screenshot may return non-public data. The current page can also be attacker-controlled web content, so the screenshot can contain attacker-authored content.
